name: Full-Body Kettlebell Circuit — Pass-to-Squat → Lunge Knee-Drive → Snatch → Press-to-March
description:
A four-move full-body kettlebell circuit on a single bell: around-the-body pass to squat, reverse lunge to knee drive, snatch, and single-arm press to march.

**This is a CIRCUIT, not a continuous flow.** Each move runs for its own rep count, then you move to the next — the beats don't feed into each other the way a Conti flow's do. Low-and-explosive conditioning; a close sibling to the Asgooch cardio complex (row/clean/squat/snatch), same intent with a snatch as the centerpiece.

The four moves are deliberately mixed: two are **leg-athletic and coordination-led** (the pass-to-squat, the lunge-to-knee-drive) and two are **overhead and core-led** (the snatch, the press-to-march). That balance is what makes it full-body conditioning rather than a leg burner or a shoulder burner.

Round count is not stated in the source; 3 is the conventional read.
flowNotes:
**A CIRCUIT, not a continuous flow** — run each move for its full rep count, then move to the next with minimal rest. Rest ~60s between rounds; 3 rounds total.

Single light-to-moderate bell: this is conditioning, so pick a load you can keep moving with for three rounds, not a bell you have to fight. The source overlays read x20 / x10 / x10 / x10; the unilateral moves are written per-side — scale to total reps if that's too much.

**The snatch is the technical centerpiece** — hips drive it, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch, no bang on the wrist. If the right shoulder crackles on the catch, swap snatches for high pulls and keep the round moving.

flowSequence.notes: Pass the bell around the body once, then squat, then pass again. Torso tall and STILL during the pass — the bell orbits, you don't. Full depth on the squat. Alternate the pass direction.

Step back into a reverse lunge, then drive the back knee forward and UP to a tall, balanced stand before stepping back again. Drive through the front heel. Stay tall through the knee drive — don't fold forward to meet the knee.

The technical centerpiece. Hips drive the bell, the arm only guides. Punch the hand THROUGH at the top so the bell rolls onto the back of the forearm instead of banging the wrist. Right-shoulder watch on the catch — sub high pulls if it crackles.

Press the bell overhead with the shoulder packed DOWN, lock it out, then march alternate knees while keeping the bell stacked STILL overhead. The obliques fight to keep the torso square under the offset load — a quiet lockout under a moving leg is the whole skill.

tips: Single bell throughout. Conditioning intent — pick a load you can keep moving with for 3 rounds, not a 1-rep-max bell.
**It's a circuit, not a flow** — each move runs for its own reps, then you move on. Minimal rest between moves, ~60s between rounds.
The snatch is the technical centerpiece: hip drive, punch-through, soft catch. If the right shoulder complains, swap snatches for high pulls.

Sibling to the Asgooch cardio complex — same low-and-explosive full-body conditioning. Belongs on a **Tuesday** strength/conditioning rotation or a Saturday cardio choice; **NOT Thursday** — the snatches and lunge knee-drives would pre-fatigue Friday legs.
